input.story: As a registered user, I want to upload a profile photo so that other users can recognise me.
input.context: Profile page. Accepted formats: JPEG and PNG. Maximum size 2 MB. The photo is cropped to a square.

criteria.text: Given the user is on the profile page, When the user selects a JPEG photo under 2 megabytes And uploads the photo, Then the photo is cropped to a square And saved And shown on the profile
Given the user is on the profile page, When the user selects a PNG photo under 2 megabytes And uploads the photo, Then the photo is cropped to a square And saved And shown on the profile
Given the user is on the profile page, When the user selects a photo larger than 2 megabytes And uploads the photo, Then the upload is rejected with a message about the 2 MB limit
When the user selects a file in a format other than JPEG or PNG, Then the upload is rejected with a message

test_cases.title: A JPEG under the size limit is saved
test_cases.expected: The photo is cropped to a square and shown on the profile

test_cases.title: A PNG under the size limit is saved
test_cases.expected: The photo is cropped to a square and shown on the profile

test_cases.title: A photo over the size limit is refused
test_cases.expected: The page shows a message about the 2 MB limit

test_cases.title: A file in another format is refused
test_cases.expected: The page shows: Use a JPEG or PNG image

add_tests.title: An executable renamed to .jpg is refused
steps: Upload avatar.jpg, which is really a non-image file
Upload a text file renamed to photo.png
Upload a real JPEG to confirm the happy path still works
add_tests.expected: Both disguised files are refused with a message about the file type, nothing is written to storage, and the real JPEG still uploads.

add_tests.title: A 0-byte file is refused with a readable message
add_tests.expected: The upload is refused with a message saying the file is empty; no broken image placeholder is stored and the previous avatar is still shown.

add_tests.title: A small file with enormous pixel dimensions is handled, not crashed on
steps: Watch the response and the server memory while it is processed
add_tests.expected: Either the image is refused with a message about its dimensions or it is resized successfully; the request returns within the normal time and the server does not run out of memory.
add_tests.test_data: large.png, 20000 x 20000 pixels, well under the size limit

add_tests.title: An upload interrupted by a lost connection reports the failure
steps: Start uploading an image and cut the network connection part way through
Restore the connection and read the page
add_tests.expected: The page shows a clear failure message and offers a retry, the old avatar is unchanged, and the retry completes normally.
add_tests.test_data: a file large enough to still be uploading when the connection is cut

add_tests.title: Cancelling a running upload leaves the old avatar in place
steps: Start uploading a large image and press Cancel while the progress bar is moving
Upload a small image to confirm the control still works
add_tests.expected: The upload stops, the old avatar is still shown, no partial file appears in storage and the next upload succeeds.
add_tests.test_data: a file large enough to show a progress bar, cancelled part way

add_tests.title: Boundary values at 1.99 MB / 2.01 MB (AC-1)
steps: Select a JPEG photo of 1.99 MB.
Select a JPEG photo of 2.01 MB.
add_tests.expected: At 1.99 MB: the photo is cropped to a square; saved; shown on the profile. At 2.01 MB: the upload is rejected with a message about the 2 MB limit (AC-3).
